newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD finds large gold deposit - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD finds large gold deposit - paper.

text.p: Brazil state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) has discovered a new deposit in Para state which contains at least 300 tonnes of gold and a further 300 tonnes of copper, local Globo newspaper said Friday.

CVRD officials were not immediately available to comment on the report but a spokeswoman for the Mines and Metals Secretariat in the Mines and Energy Ministry said a CVRD subsidiary was preparing an official statement.

The new reserve is said to be in the region of Igarape-Bahia, currently CVRD's largest operational gold mine, and 150 kilometers from Serra Pelada, scene of the world's largest gold rush in the 1980s.
If confirmed, the deposit would be twice the size of estimated reserves so far at Serra Leste, the deposit announced with much fanfare by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in February this year.
At the time, the Serra Leste deposit was put at 150 tonnes but expectations are reserves could be higher at deeper levels.

CVRD was forced to stop further surveys at Serra Leste in May this year because of protests by wildcat gold miners who claim Serra Leste's proximity to Serra Pelada means they should have a share of future profits.
After months of standoff, the federal government sent in troops on Thursday to reclaim the mine peacefully and CVRD is hoping to resume work as soon as possible.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
